title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 140
paragraphs: The Athenians had sent men to Delphi to consult the oracle. After these had performed the usual rites in the sacred precinct, when they had entered the inner sanctuary and taken their seats, the Pythian priestess — whose name was Aristonice — uttered this oracle to them:

“Why do you sit, you wretched ones? Flee to the uttermost limits, leaving your home and the heights of the wheel-round city behind you! Lo, there remains now neither head nor body in safety — neither the feet below, nor the hands, nor anything between is left to you; all are destroyed together, for fire and the passionate War-god, driving on the Syrian car at speed, shall hurl them down to ruin. Not yours alone — he shall make many other great strongholds perish, yes, he shall deliver many temples of the gods to the ravening fire: temples that even now stand with the sweat of their terror streaming down, shaking with dread; and lo! from the topmost roof to the pavement dark blood trickles, foretelling the dire, unavoidable evil. Forth from the shrine with you, and steep your soul in sorrow!”
